transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My sleep is completely off—I either lie awake most of the night or crash at odd hours and still wake up exhausted. It's just gotten really hard to function during the day when I'm this tired all the time.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you also been feeling down or losing interest in things, or is the main problem feeling worried or tense when you try to sleep?

It's definitely not just the sleep; I've also been feeling really down and have completely lost interest in things I used to love. I used to paint, organize brunches, and volunteer, but now even replying to a friend's text feels too exhausting and pointless.

When you can’t sleep, is it mostly because your mind is racing with worry or tension, or do you still have trouble sleeping even when you don’t feel especially anxious? Also, did the sleep problems start before the low mood and loss of interest, or after?

When I lie awake, my mind is definitely racing for hours, and I often wake up early feeling really wired and panicky. The sleep issues and the low mood started around the same time, building up together shortly after my breakup and some family conflicts about two years ago.

During the day, even when you’re not trying to sleep, do you spend most days feeling excessively worried or on edge about different things and find it hard to control the worry? Or is the low mood and loss of interest the main problem most of the time?

While my mind definitely races when I'm trying to sleep at night, during the day the main issue is definitely the heavy, low mood and a complete loss of interest in everything. I don't really feel constantly worried or on edge about different things; it's more that I feel empty, exhausted, and completely unmotivated.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life? If yes, have you had any plan or intent to act on those thoughts?

When I'm feeling really down and replaying all my mistakes, I do sometimes think that everyone would be better off if I just disappeared. I don't have any actual plans or intent to hurt myself, but the feeling of being a burden is just incredibly heavy.

Do your low mood and loss of interest still feel closely tied to the breakup and family conflict, getting worse when those problems flare up? Or have they taken on a life of their own and stayed present most days even when those stressors aren’t actively happening?

They have definitely taken on a life of their own at this point. Even though the breakup and family fights started it all, this heavy, hopeless feeling has been there almost constantly for over two years, regardless of how things are going with them. I honestly can't even remember the last time I actually felt like myself.
During these past two years, have there been any periods lasting at least 2 months when your mood felt mostly back to normal? Or has the depression been there nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any long stretches of feeling back to normal, and the depression has been there almost every single day for the last two years. At most, I had a brief couple of weeks last fall where my mood felt somewhat neutral, but that heavy, hopeless feeling always returned quickly.

During these two years, have there ever been periods lasting at least 2 weeks when your depression became much worse than your usual baseline, with symptoms like very poor appetite or weight change, slowed movement, intense guilt, or being unable to function? Or has it stayed at about the same steady level the whole time?

Actually, those symptoms have pretty much been my steady baseline for the last two years rather than just temporary spikes. I constantly struggle to eat, feel like I'm moving through molasses, and carry this intense guilt and inability to function almost every day. While some days are definitely heavier than others, this low, draining state has been my constant reality since shortly after the breakup.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or were more impulsive than normal? Even if it felt productive or happened before the depression started.

No, I’ve never had periods where I felt abnormally revved up, euphoric, or needed very little sleep while still feeling rested. I used to be a naturally energetic and creative person before the depression hit, but I've never experienced those kinds of impulsive high-energy phases. When I stay awake now, it's just because my mind is racing and it leaves me completely exhausted, not energized.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronic depressive syndrome present nearly every day for over two years, without any remission lasting 2 months, and without a history of manic or hypomanic episodes. Symptoms include persistent low mood, marked anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue, poor appetite, psychomotor slowing, hopelessness, guilt, passive death wishes, and significant functional impairment. Because this depressive picture has been continuous for more than two years as a steady baseline rather than clearly separated recurrent episodes, persistent mood disorder/dysthymia is the best fit among the provided options.
